settings.toolchains.hint.text: Paths to devkitPro and mgba : required for Build & Run.

settings.theme.note.text: Only one theme exists today : no light/dark toggle or variant for now.

settings.shortcuts.hint.text: Click a key and type the new combination. Two actions on the same key are flagged in red — both stay active, only the first declared in the context responds.

settings.external.note.text: Third-party software to edit assets, not yet wired to an 'Edit externally' button in the screens, just recorded here.

home.empty.text:
No recent project.
Create a new project or open an existing folder.

home.clear_tip.text: Removes entries pointing to projects that can't be found

home.load_tip.text: Browse the disk for an existing project folder

home.status.explain_devkitpro.text: the compilation toolchain (ARM + grit) that turns your project into a playable .gba ROM

home.status.explain_mgba.text: the emulator used to launch and test your ROM directly from the editor

uiinsp.priority.tip.text:
OBJ depth, when this element renders as a sprite (its node follows an actor).

Auto inherits the actor's depth, live.
0 = frontmost … 3 = backmost overrides it.

uiinsp.text.content_tip.text: Written into the text table, not into the element — the same entry is editable from the Text screen. Markup accepted ([speed=…], $var…).

uiinsp.text.entry_tip.text: Bind this element to another existing entry — to share one label between several screens.

uiinsp.text.sample_tip.text: Editor only: used to measure overflow, never compiled — the script decides the displayed text.

uiinsp.text.bank_tip.text:
UI palette bank — SHARED by every text of this scene.

A background can pick its bank per element (the hardware selects it tile by tile, at no cost). Text can't: a glyph is recolored into VRAM once per color index, so every text must agree on the same bank — one more bank would mean one more full copy.

Same setting as the Scene inspector; changing it here changes it for the whole scene.

uiinsp.text.ink_tip.text:
Ink — the color of the glyphs, an index in the scene's UI palette bank.

Font ink keeps the font's own shades (outline, fill).
Any other value flattens the ink to that single color.

Each color used costs one more copy of the scene's glyphs in VRAM.

uiinsp.text.highlight_tip.text:
Highlight — a color laid UNDER the text, on the tiles it actually covers.

By default a text already sits on its container's background. A highlight overrides it, marker-style, on the written extent only.

Composing costs a block of surface tiles for the scene, whatever the font — a background or a highlight both pay it once.

uiinsp.fill.sprite_tip.text: Sprite tiled across the panel. Unlike an image, the panel keeps its own size: the sprite repeats to cover it, one OAM slot per cell (the hardware cannot stretch an OBJ without affine mode).

uiinsp.fill.state_tip.text: Initial animation state. A script can change it later with ui.image_set — a panel background gets an IMAGE_* constant of its own, like any image.

uiinsp.fill.speed_tip.text:
Frames between two animation frames, overriding the state's own speed.

0 (= From sprite) keeps the value edited in the Sprite Editor, which stays the single source of truth — otherwise fixing a speed there would silently stop having any effect here.

uiinsp.list.selection_tip.text:
Selection — whether this list reads the D-pad.

An inactive list stays on screen and keeps its current item; it just stops moving. That is what lets a menu and its submenu show at once — without it, both walk on the same press.

Hiding the list is a different thing: it disappears.

uiinsp.list.columns_tip.text:
Columns — how wide one line of the grid is.

1 column is a plain vertical list. Set it to the number of rows for a row of tabs, or to any width for a grid.

Scrolling moves by a whole LINE, so the columns an author laid out stay where they are.

uiinsp.list.order_tip.text:
Order — the direction item numbers run in.

Column first: top to bottom, then the next column.
Row first: left to right, then the line below.

With a single column both describe the same walk; the other axis of the D-pad is then left to the game.

uiinsp.list.cursor_tip.text:
Cursor — an Image of this layout that the list moves onto the selected row.

Place it facing the FIRST row: the engine offsets it by the distance between that row and the current one, so the layout stays the truth.

No cursor is a valid choice — the selected row can be marked by its style instead.

uiinsp.list.motion_tip.text: Motion — Snap puts the cursor on the row at once; Slide travels the distance at the speed below.

uiinsp.list.ink_tip.text:
Ink of the SELECTED row — an index in the scene's UI palette bank, like a text's own ink.

Leaving it at the default keeps whatever each row already uses. Each color costs one more copy of the scene's glyphs in VRAM.

uiinsp.list.highlight_tip.text:
Highlight of the SELECTED row — a color laid under its text, on the extent it covers.

The classic way to mark a menu selection without a cursor.

uiinsp.img.sprite_tip.text: Sprite asset drawn here. Picking one resizes the element to its frame — the hardware cannot stretch a sprite.

uiinsp.img.state_tip.text: State shown when the scene starts. A script can switch to any other state of this sprite — ui.image_set("name", "state").

uiinsp.img.play_tip.text: A frozen image costs no per-frame work and never rewrites the tilemap — the right default for a static HUD icon.

uiinsp.bank_inherited_tip.text: Read-only: this text sits in a filled container and reads its ink from the container's bank. Change it through the container's fill.

actorinsp.empty.text:
Select an actor
from the left panel

actorinsp.sprite_preview_tip.text:
Starting sprite

Click to assign a sprite from the project.
First frame of the initial AnimState.

actorinsp.index_tip.text: Position of the actor in the scene (processing and render order).

actorinsp.relink_tip.text:
Reload this instance's components/palette/notes from the
prefab's current definition — discards local structural changes.

actorinsp.expose_tip.text:
Push this instance's components/palette/notes up to the prefab —
every OTHER instance of it is updated too.

actorinsp.unlink_tip.text:
Break the link with the prefab
(the actor becomes independent)

actorinsp.expose_new_tip.text:
Create a new prefab from this actor's current components/palette/
notes — this actor becomes its first linked instance.

actorinsp.parent_tip.text:
Parent

The actor in whose frame this one's position is expressed.
X/Y, rotation and scale then become LOCAL: the parent
moves, turns or grows, and its subtree follows.

This is not inheritance — the definition is not reused. For that,
use a prefab. Hiding the parent hides its whole subtree.

A parent is chosen in the same scene, and a cycle is refused at Build.

actorinsp.children_tip.text:
The CHILDREN of this prefab — a segmented boss, a caterpillar.
Each child is a full actor: its sprite, its boxes, its local
transform. Double-click to edit one, drag-and-drop ONTO another
child to reparent it.

The pool is counted in INSTANCES: max instances × (1 + children)
entries are reserved, and that total is what you pay.

sceneinsp.backdrop_tip.text:
Backdrop color

Index 0 of the BG palette — shown wherever no layer or
sprite draws, including through a window that masks everything.

Quantized to BGR555 (5 bits per channel) like on hardware.

sceneinsp.backdrop_reset_tip.text: Reuse the backdrop color defined at project level

sceneinsp.transition_tip.text:
Fade played when leaving AND when opening this scene

Each scene describes its own disappearance and its own appearance,
so two scenes never fight over a switch.

The outgoing scene is frozen while its fade plays, and this scene's
color blending is suspended for the duration — the hardware has a
single blend mode, there is no fade on top of a translucency.

sceneinsp.transition_frames_tip.text: Frames per half — leaving, then opening.

sceneinsp.music_tip.text:
Track started when this scene opens

Keep playing — the scene issues no order at all, so whatever is
already playing carries on. This is the default: walking through a
door should not restart the theme.

Silence — explicitly stops the music.

The track starts before the scene's on_start, so a music.play()
in the script overrides it.

sceneinsp.no_bitmap_text.text: Import an image in Bitmap mode first, in the Background Editor.

sceneinsp.ui_layer_tip.text:
Layer reserved for HUD text (TTE)

In-game text (score, dialogue…) takes up a whole BG layer.
Pick a BG that isn't used by a background.

Conflict ⚠: if this BG is already assigned to a background,
the two overlap and the result is undefined.

sceneinsp.fallback_add.text: Choose a fallback font for this scene

sceneinsp.scene_actors_tip.text:
Entries reserved for the actors placed in this scene.

0 = automatic: the reservation follows what you actually place. Set it higher than the placed count only if you need headroom.

sceneinsp.no_prefab.text: No prefab in this project yet — nothing to pool.

sceneinsp.pool_tip.text:
How many '{name}' can be alive at once in this scene.

0 = this scene never spawns it, and pays nothing for it.

sceneinsp.pool_tip_parts.text: This prefab has {n} part(s), so one instance costs {slots} slots.

sceneinsp.text_bg_conflict_tip.text: BG{n} carries '{name}' — will be overwritten by the text

sndmix.start_tip.text:
The state active when the game starts.

It is baked into the ROM: without it, no action would resolve to anything before the first sound.set_state().

sndmix.matrix_hint.text: An animation frame cites an ACTION; the active state says which {kind} it points to. A cell left at 'none' plays nothing in that state — a footstep doesn't sound mid-air.

sndmix.matrix_hint_empty.text: No action yet. Add one, then drop its name on a frame in the Sprite Editor: that's what makes the same walk cycle usable on several grounds.

sndmix.new_action_prompt.text: Name (the one the frames will carry):

sndmix.graph_del_tip.text: Delete what is selected — a state or a transition (Del)

sndmix.auto_layout_tip.text: Arrange the nodes in columns, from the start state.

sndmix.graph_hint_empty.text: No music state. '+ State' creates one.

sndmix.graph_hint_no_trans.text: Drag the dot on a node's right edge to another to create a transition; click a wire then Del to cut it.

sndmix.trigger_tip.text:
The name the script emits: sound.trigger("…").

The graph DECLARES this vocabulary — a trigger unknown here is refused by the checker instead of staying silent in-game.

sndmix.kind_tip.text:
The FADE works between any two tracks, at the price of a dip.
The CUT resumes the other track at the same position, without a dip — but
the two tracks must share the same structure.

sndmix.frames_tip.text: Fade duration, in frames (60 per second).

sndmix.start_state_tip.text: The state active when the game starts — one per machine.

sndmix.intensity_tip.text:
What the intensity DRIVES, named explicitly.

The hardware has only three continuous knobs: the module's volume,
its tempo and its pitch. Going from DRUMLESS to the full track is not
one of them — that's another STATE, not a slider.

sndmix.ivalue_tip.text: 100 % = neutral value. Tempo and pitch are clamped to ×0.5–×2 by the hardware.

bgedit.kind_scene_tip.text: Scene decor — placed as a layer, repainted per tile

bgedit.kind_ui_tip.text: Interface — fills a UI panel as a stretchable frame or a plain image

bgedit.kind_animated_tip.text: Animation sheet — cut into frames and dropped onto another background

bgedit.tiled_tip.text: Tiled background (Mode 0) — tileset + tilemap, scroll, inpainting

bgedit.bitmap_tip.text: Full-screen bitmap ≤240×160, no tiles (photos / title screens)

bgedit.d8_tip.text: 256 colors, one palette (rich pixel-art / bitmap Mode 4)

bgedit.d16_tip.text: 15-bit direct color (true-color photos) — coming soon, falls back to Mode 4

bgedit.nine_tip.text: Stretchable frame: fixed corners, repeated edges and center

bgedit.plain_tip.text: Plain image, laid top-left and cropped to the panel

bgedit.speed_tip.text: Ticks (1/60 s) between two frames — same unit as a sprite animation speed.

bgedit.per_instance_tip.text: Each copy placed on a background animates on its own.

bgedit.shared_tip.text: Every copy animates together, in step.

bgedit.src_hint.text: Drag onto the canvas to place

bgedit.anim_source_tip.text: {name} — {n} frame(s). Drag onto the canvas to place it.

bgedit.pl_start_tip.text: Which frame this copy starts on. Lets two copies of the same animation sit at different points of the loop.

bgedit.pl_speed_tip.text: Ticks between two frames for this copy only. Leave at default to follow the animation's own speed.

bgedit.restore_tip.text: Resets the background to its first import (PNG re-compression) — added palettes and painting will be lost.

bgedit.extract_tip.text: Promotes palettes deduced from the PNG into shared catalog palettes (visible and editable from the Palette Editor). Created palettes are assigned to this background.

bgedit.limit_text.text: A background can only have 16 palettes.

bgedit.del_pal_text.text:
Remove palette {idx}?
Tiles using it will fall back to palette 0.

bgedit.restore_dialog_text.text:
Reset this background to its very first import?
Added palettes and painting (inpainting) will be lost.

bgedit.restore_no_png_text.text: Source PNG not found — restoration impossible.

bgedit.no_extract_text.text: This background doesn't have a palette to extract yet (uncompressed or unreadable image).

sndpanel.volume_tip.text:
Level, as a percentage.

maxmod has two volume scales — 0–255 for an effect, 0–1024 for the module — and the build converts to the target's. A percentage can't be confused with either.

sndpanel.rate_tip.text:
Target sample rate for this effect.

Conversion happens at build: the file in assets/ is never rewritten, so you can raise the rate afterwards without losing anything.

'From project' follows the project setting.

sndpanel.music_weight_shared.text: In ROM: {kb} KiB own, plus {shared} KiB of samples shared with {n} other track(s).  (last build)

sndpanel.box_tip.text:
The game loads only ONE per family — the first by name.

The others stay in the project but won't sound; the validator flags them.

sndpanel.right_empty.text:
Select or create
an SFX or a track
to edit its properties

sndpanel.rom_play_tip.text:
Plays the MusicBox as the ROM will play it.

Clicking a node emits the trigger that leads to it: the transition sounds exactly as in-game, without a build. If no edge leads to that node, nothing happens — as on the console.

sndpanel.musicbox_empty.text: A MusicBox arranges musical states and the transitions between them: which track in which mood, and by which trigger you move from one to another.

sndpanel.soundbox_empty.text: A SoundBox says which effect each action points to per state — the same walk cycle sounds sand or gravel without being authored twice.

sndpanel.jinglebox_empty.text: A JingleBox says which module each jingle action points to per state. A jingle layers over the music, it doesn't replace it.

sprframe.preview_indexed_tip.text: Preview: recolored by the PALETTE strip's active palette (in-game render)

sprframe.flip_x_tip.text: Horizontal flip of the active brush (Shift+X)

sprframe.flip_y_tip.text: Vertical flip of the active brush (Shift+Y)

sprpanel.import_replace_tip.text: Choose an image, validate and encode it (GBA, non-destructive) and attach it to the current sprite.

sprpanel.extract_tip.text: Creates a catalog palette “pal_<name>” from the PNG's colors (index 0 = transparency, then darkest to lightest).

comped.sfx_tip.text:
Sfx played by this component.
Add sounds from the Sound Mixer screen to see them appear here.

comped.trigger_tip.text:
manual — plays nothing automatically, call self:play_sfx() from a script.
on_spawn — plays when the actor starts, without a script.
on_destroy — plays just before the actor is destroyed (by itself or another), without a script on this actor.
button — plays while the actor is active and that button is held, without a script. Handy for a menu item.

comped.palette_tip.text: “No palette” = original PNG colors (default). Otherwise, choose one of the scene's active palettes ("Active palettes" card in the scene inspector).

comped.anim_speed_tip.text:
Animation speed

GBA ticks (60 fps) between two frames, for the initial state ({state}) only.
8 ticks ≈ 7.5 fps | 4 = 15 fps | 2 = 30 fps

Other states keep their own speed — adjustable in the Sprite Editor.

comped.affine_tip.text:
Reserves one of the GBA's 32 affine matrix slots for this sprite, even at identity.

On → the sprite can rotate and scale: the actor's world rotation/scale (Transform card) become visible, and the three local settings below are composed on top — rotation ADDED, scale MULTIPLIED, offset expressed in the actor's frame.

Off → plain OAM, no slot. The actor's rotation and scale still read and write from scripts, but nothing draws them.

GBA: OAM attribute 1, bits 8-12 (affine matrix slot).

comped.scale_x_tip.text: Local X scale — MULTIPLIED by the actor's scale (affine OAM). Requires Affine transform above.

comped.scale_y_tip.text: Local Y scale — MULTIPLIED by the actor's scale (affine OAM). Requires Affine transform above.

comped.rotation_tip.text: Local rotation in degrees — ADDED to the actor's rotation (affine OAM). Requires Affine transform above.

comped.offset_x_tip.text: Offset X from the actor — in the actor's LOCAL frame, in pixels. The sprite has no world position: it is drawn at the actor's position + this offset, rotated/scaled with the actor. Requires Affine transform above.

comped.offset_y_tip.text: Offset Y from the actor — in the actor's LOCAL frame, in pixels. Requires Affine transform above.

datagrid.empty.text:
No table selected.

A data table is read from a script as data.Name[i].column — its rows are numbered from 1, like every array in Lua.

datagrid.no_column_text.text: Add a column first — a row has nowhere to go.

datagrid.rename_text.text: '{name}' is not usable: a column is written as code in scripts (data.{table}[i].{col}), so it must be a plain identifier — letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit — and unique within the table.

scttree.iface_tip_shared.text:
Interface “{name}”
SHARED by {n} scenes — editing it affects all of them.

win.about_text.text: GBA Editor - homebrew Game Boy Advance

win.actor_not_found.text: '{name}' not found in the active scene

win.screen_contract.text: '{name}' does not fulfill the ProjectScreen contract (no load_project) — the screen will receive no project.

win.build_no_scene.text: Add at least one scene before building

win.oam_tip.text:
OAM — Object Attribute Memory
The GBA can show 128 sprites at once.
Beyond that, extra sprites don't appear.
Each visible actor uses 1 OAM slot per frame.

win.scanline_tip.text:
OBJ budget per scanline (GBA)
The hardware has 1210 cycles per line to draw the
sprites; a regular object costs about its width in pixels
(a rotated/scaled object: 2 × width + 10).
Beyond that, the next objects in OAM order aren't drawn.
Value = worst line on screen, sprite-target text zones included.

win.vram_tip.text:
Sprite VRAM — OBJ area
The sprite VRAM area holds 1024 8×8 tiles (16KB in 16-color mode).
A 16×16 sprite uses 4 tiles, a 32×32 uses 16.

win.pal_tip.text:
Sprite palettes
The GBA has 16 palettes of 16 colors for sprites.
Each color is 15-bit (32,768 possible colors).
Color 0 of each palette is transparent.

win.gba_info_tip.text:
Game Boy Advance — hardware specifications
CPU  : ARM7TDMI @ 16.78 MHz
RAM  : 256 KB external WRAM + 32 KB internal IRAM
VRAM : 96 KB total
Screen: 240×160 pixels, 15-bit color
Sound: 2 DirectSound PCM channels + 4 legacy GB channels

palgrid.empty.text: Select a palette from the left panel

colins.snap_tip.text: Color snapped to the GBA's 15-bit grid (5 bits/channel)

fontinsp.bg_tip.text:
BACKGROUND color of the sheet.

A sheet exported without an alpha channel lands on a flat fill — green,
magenta, white. Without designating it, the encoder mistakes it for ink
and every glyph comes out as a solid block.

Suggested automatically on import (dominant color); re-pick it
if the sheet is atypical.

fontinsp.space_tip.text:
Color that MARKS THE SPACING between glyphs.

A convention used by several tools, including GB Studio: a second color
fills the end of each cell to indicate where the character ends.
It must disappear just like the background, or it will show up
in-game.

fontinsp.pick_tip.text: Pick the “{name}” color from the sheet

fontinsp.clear_tip.text: No longer make the “{name}” color transparent

fontinsp.charset_tip.text:
Characters covered by this font — derived from the glyphs,
never stored as such.

Editable: leaving the box reassigns characters to the cells
in order (character 1 → cell 1, …). One cell holds one
character, so a ligature (e.g. “...”) is set cell by cell,
not here.

fontinsp.charset_hint.text: Editing reassigns characters to cells in order. Extra cells keep their character; ligatures are set cell by cell.

fontinsp.char_tip.text:
This cell's character

Multiple characters are accepted (e.g. “...”): the cell then
becomes a ligature, a single drawing for a sequence of
characters.

fontinsp.glyph_hint.text: Glyphs are drawn in your image editor, just like for a sprite — here you only correct which character each cell corresponds to.

fontinsp.key_none.text: No transparent color — the sheet is used as-is.

fontinsp.key_count.one: {n} color made transparent. The PNG is not modified.
fontinsp.key_count.other: {n} colors made transparent. The PNG is not modified.

fontinsp.adv_mono.text: Mono advance — designating the spacing makes it proportional.

glsheet.hint_default.text: Click a cell then type the character it represents — the selection advances on its own. Arrows to navigate.

glsheet.merge_tip.text:
Merges the selected cells into ONE glyph covering their
rectangle — a 16×16 font in an 8×8 sheet, or a
wide pictogram for an entire word.

Shift+click a second cell to extend the selection.

glsheet.reslice_tip.text:
Re-slices the sheet at this cell size.
Assigned characters are reset from scratch — use this
when the detected grid is wrong, not for fine adjustment.

glsheet.pick_hint.text: Click the {name} color on the sheet — Escape to cancel.

mktool.wraps.text: Wraps the selection — click again to remove it.

mktool.dropped.text: Dropped in front of the selection, which is left intact.

mktool.value_tip.text:
$name
Inserts the value of a project global or constant, read at display time.

txtinsp.empty.text:
Select a text entry
from the table

txtinsp.note_tip.text: Context intended for translation (v0.8) — never shown in-game.

txttbl.unused_tip.text: Entries no script and no layout refers to

txttbl.group_tip.text:
Group by category — folds the table back into its filing.
Sorting then applies inside each group.

txttbl.add_tip.text: New text (filed where the selection is)

txttbl.group_root_tip.text:
Texts filed at the root — this is the absence of a category,
not a name: it cannot be renamed. File them from the level 1
field below.

txttbl.group_rename_tip.text:
Double-click to rename this category — it renames the filing of
every text it contains.

txttbl.sec_tip.text:
Filing — accents, spaces and duplicates allowed.
Never resolved, never referenced: it organizes the table
and suggests the key, without ever owning it.

txttbl.key_hand.text: Named by hand — independent of the filing

txttbl.key_dblclick.text: Double-click to name it by hand.

txttbl.used_unknown_tip.text: Scripts could not be parsed — usage is unknown, not zero.

txttbl.unused_cell_tip.text: No script and no layout refers to this key.

txtwb.copy_tip.text: Copy the key — paste into a Lua script

txtwb.filing_tip.text:
Filing — accents, spaces and duplicates allowed.
Never resolved, never referenced: it organizes the table and
suggests the key, without ever owning it.

txtwb.preview_font_tip.text: Font used for the preview (doesn't affect the text)

txtwb.multi_ph.text: Content is edited one entry at a time

txtwb.empty_ph.text: Select a text entry to edit its content…

txtwb.key_tip_head.text: Key — the handle Lua scripts write, resolved at build time.

txtwb.key_tip_auto.text:
It DERIVES from the filing and will follow it. Unlock to
name it by hand: it will detach from it permanently.

txtwb.key_tip_hand.text:
Named by hand: the filing no longer affects it.
Renaming it updates the scripts that reference it.

txtwb.lock_attached.text: Key attached to the filing — click to name it by hand

txtwb.lock_reattach.text: Click to re-attach it to the filing

txtwb.lock_hand.text: Named by hand — click to re-attach it to the filing

txtpnl.invalid_key_msg.text: “{name}” is empty or already used by another text.

txtpnl.delete_msg.text:
Delete {what}?

Scripts that use them will no longer compile.

txtscr.reslice_confirm_msg.text:
Re-slice “{name}” into {cw}×{ch} cells?

Assigned characters are reset from scratch — manual corrections will be lost.

fsprev.backdrop_tip.text:
Proof background — currently {name}.
Click for {next}.

Reading aid only: it changes nothing in the text or in the ROM.

scrsb.bg_ref.text: Editorial reference — a background is placed in the scene, not from a script.

vartbl.array_tip.text:
Array size — number of cells, indexed from 1 (global.name[1]..[N]).
Right-click → Array to turn it back into a single value.
